conventions.convention: The inner product is linear in its first argument. The coefficient of v_b in D_j^ch v_a is c_j = ⟨D_j^ch v_a,v_b⟩; M = Σ_j c_j g_j uses these coefficients without conjugation.

W is a declared finite-dimensional subspace of D(H_κ) ∩ D(Q_1) ∩ D(Q_2) ∩ D(Q_3). H_a and D_i^W are compressions; channel matrices are real Cartesian combinations D_j^ch = Σ_i e_{j,i}D_i^W. The d=0 branch has no levels or normalized preparations.
Radiation uses transverse L²(R³;C³) vectors, ε(k)=ℏc|k|, cutoff support 0<ε≤Λ, and g_j/√ε ∈ h. Energies are in joules, times in seconds, and the interaction is declared to have energy units.
The coupled model calls Δ=E_a−E_b>0 an upward level pair, meaning a lies above b. The stimulated-drive calculation instead uses Δ=E_k−E_i for input i and output k.
P_t is a formal normalized kernel law for M≠0 and t>0, including zero coupling. Normalizing the physical emission vector additionally requires η_0≠0. No normalized law is asserted for M=0.
Golden-rule and concentration claims use an L¹ density representative continuous at Δ; concentration additionally requires 0<Δ<Λ and J_b(Δ)>0. The golden-rule theorem excludes Δ=Λ.
The prescribed field is continuous on a compact time interval and drives H_d(t)=H_a−Σ_j E_ext,j(t)D_j^W. The long-wavelength criterion is qualitative, with no claimed phase-error bound.

Spherical components are Q_0=X_3 and Q_±=(X_1±iX_2)/√2, without the alternative spherical-tensor minus sign. The charge magnitude q_el>0 is distinct from the component index q∈{−1,0,1}; D_q=−q_el Q_q.

The spectral comparison assumes that J_1 and J_2 are not proportional almost everywhere, as well as having equal positive values at Δ. Its discriminator concerns model laws, with no finite-sample discrimination guarantee.

load_bearing.statement: The declared finite-level cutoff dipole model is the Hilbert space C^d ⊗ F(h) with H_LM = H_a ⊗ I + I ⊗ H_f + η_0 Σ_j D_j^ch ⊗ φ(g_j), on C^d ⊗ D(H_f), using the declared Coulomb compressions and cutoff channel data.

Under the stated choice, transverse-space and cutoff hypotheses, |A_b(k,t)|² = η_0² t K_t(ε(k)−Δ)‖M(k)‖². For M≠0 and every t>0 the normalized kernel law exists; under a continuous positive density at 0<Δ<Λ it concentrates at Δ, and positive-measure windows with positive density have positive probability at every t>0.
Defines Δ, c_j, M, ν_b, A_b and γ_b=‖A_b‖²; defines the normalized single-vertex law for M≠0 and t>0, and its ideal energy-window Born reading in the normalized one-photon preparation when η_0≠0.

For the declared upward level pair, the level-b one-photon component of the first Dyson term is v_b ⊗ A_b. On 0≤t≤T, |p_b(t)−γ_b(t)|≤ε_2(t)(2‖A_b‖+ε_2(t)); reverse first-order amplitudes for the same unit photon vector obey α_abs=−conjugate(α_em).

For the declared prescribed dipole drive, proves the first-order amplitude with its Dyson remainder, the sinusoidal component formulas, equal reverse-transition first-order squared moduli, and the conditional identification of the specified Pauli data with the circular and linear drive families.

For the declared Coulomb bound states, dipole pairings are absolutely convergent and factor radially and angularly; nonvanishing requires l′=l±1 and m′=m+q, hence opposite parity. The vanishing conditions transfer entry by entry to a finite bound-state subfamily with its selected orthonormal basis.

Under the stated density and continuity hypotheses, γ_b(t)/t tends to 2πη_0²J_b(Δ)/ℏ when 0<Δ<Λ and J_b(Δ)>0, and to zero when Δ>Λ; Δ=Λ is excluded. Γ_b names the model coefficient, with no exact decay-law or measured-rate assertion.

concerns.concern: The final Remark says the first-order amplitude is 'the short-time expansion of an exactly solvable population oscillation' after identifying both circular and linear families. The circular supplier supplies an exact Rabi solution; the linear supplier supplies an averaged Rabi solution with an error bound. The linear example explicitly shows that its full first-order coefficient has four times the averaged model's leading small-time coefficient. Qualify this remark to distinguish the circular exact solution from the linear averaged comparison.

The angular summary assigns '1/√3' to the entries ⟨Y_10,Q_0Y_00⟩ and ⟨Y_1,±1,Q_±Y_00⟩. The example's clause (b) correctly gives ∓1/√3 for the latter entries: the plus-component entry is negative. The summary must distinguish signed factors from their common modulus.

The comparison summary says that two models 'whose mode densities agree at the transition energy' have different normalized photon-energy laws for every t>0. It omits the thought experiment's essential nonproportionality hypothesis. Equal densities satisfy the stated summary condition but yield identical laws. Include the actual hypothesis rather than asserting the stronger implication.

Under 'What the three items establish', the remark says two models 'whose mode densities agree at the transition energy have the same rate coefficient but different formal single-vertex photon-energy laws'. The cited thought experiment additionally assumes the densities are not proportional almost everywhere. Without that condition, J_1=J_2 is a counterexample to the summary.

Fact F3 asserts equality of measures is equivalent to equality almost everywhere of their normalized densities, citing definitions rather than proving this implication. The implication is valid, but step 1.2 needs the elementary uniqueness argument: test the integrable density difference on the measurable sets where it is positive or negative, replacing them by Borel sets modulo null sets if necessary.

seams_checked.note: The theorem's operative formulas preserve the first-order and rotating-wave supplier hypotheses, including ω≠0 and a separate ω=0 branch. Its final Remark overstates exact solvability for the linear family; see concern.
Transverse space, ε=ℏc|k|, packet normalization, free-energy law and ideal window detector retain the supplier's model and apparatus qualifications.

Cutoff and infrared integrability hypotheses are retained. Positive-dimensional self-adjointness and vacuum Dyson convergence are used in their stated regimes; d=0 is handled locally. The coefficient limit is not promoted to an exact decay law.
State, Born, autonomous, measurement and apparatus postulates remain adopted assumptions; units and inherited choice assumptions are retained.
Uses the charged relative-coordinate pair and finite-domain compressions, preserving the exclusion of the uncompressed static linear potential.
Pure preparations and density operators are used on nonzero model spaces; the zero-dimensional branch declares no normalized preparation.
Exact probabilities are Born probabilities of declared projections; γ_b is explicitly distinguished from those probabilities.
Bosonic radiation sectors are adopted through the radiation extension; no spin-statistics deduction is introduced.
Uses the self-adjoint coupled Hamiltonian's spectral unitary flow and density conjugation; prescribed drives remain separate.
The prescribed finite-dimensional Hermitian family is norm-continuous on a compact interval, satisfying the bounded Dyson supplier.
Projection and energy-window measurements are ideal declared measurements, with no destructive detector or laboratory realization inferred.
Pauli signs and harmonic representatives match the suppliers. The angular proof uses the finite harmonic span before applying the L_z differential expression.
Uses the declared relative Coulomb operator and bound-state labels; does not identify the bound family with a basis of all L².
Coordinate domains and absolutely convergent radial/angular factorization are preserved. Necessary angular restrictions are proved locally without assuming nonzero radial integrals.
The two-level example identifies the linear family and compares with the exact averaged Rabi probability using the supplier's finite-time error contract.
The example's explicit harmonics and signed angular factors agree with the normalization and Pauli suppliers. The companion page's unsigned summary is separately flagged.
Parameters are declared model data, with SI units and P7 qualifications; no measured inputs or statistical precision are invented.
Normalized model laws and ideal probabilities remain distinct from unnormalized first-order coefficients and observed frequencies.
Uses the dipole factorization and oscillator recurrence as stated; hydrogen radial factors remain unevaluated.
Hydrogenic labels and model interpretation retain the Coulomb supplier's scope, with no observed spectrum or transition intensity inferred.
Compressed dipole data are used conditionally under the finite-level model; no uncompressed Stark approximation is introduced.
Ideal energy-window probabilities use normalized one-photon preparations only at nonzero coupling; repeated-data comparison is explicitly left to a separate sampling and apparatus model.
